config.title: Color Picker

intro.title: Color Picker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive color picker application using React and TypeScript. You will learn how to manage state to track the selected color and update the UI in real-time. The core programming concept covered is handling user events, such as clicks or input changes, to control application behavior. You will use React hooks like useState for state management and TypeScript interfaces for type safety. By the end, you'll have a functional component that displays a color palette and shows the currently chosen color.
intro.usecase: Color pickers are essential UI components in any application that involves customization or design. You'll find them in graphic design tools like Figma or Canva for selecting fill and stroke colors, in e-commerce sites for customizing product colors, and in dashboard settings panels for theming and branding. As a developer, implementing a color picker is a common task when building user profile editors, admin configuration areas, or any interactive feature that allows users to personalize their visual experience.

objectives: Construct a controlled ColorPicker component using React hooks and TypeScript interfaces
Initialize and manage color state with useState hook and typed interfaces
Implement input handlers to update color values from user interactions
Configure color preview display that reflects current state changes
Bind color input controls to component state with proper TypeScript typing
Render a complete color picker interface with real-time feedback
Integrate color validation to ensure values remain within acceptable ranges

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the ColorPicker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ColorPicker that returns a JSX element. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a JSX element. For now, you can return a simple placeholder like a div or null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your ColorPicker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ColorPicker component is defined and ready to be built upon in later steps.
successCriteria: The ColorPicker component is defined as a function that returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a component named ColorPicker that returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've named it ColorPicker and it returns a JSX element.

steps.title: Define the color state with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Inside your ColorPicker component, initialize a state variable called 'color' using useState. Type it as string with an initial value of '#000000'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported. Remember to provide the type annotation for the state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [count, setCount] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed state variable 'color' initialized to '#000000'.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with type annotation <string> and initial value '#000000', and the state variable is named 'color'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct type annotation and initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax for useState with TypeScript. The state should be typed as string and initialized to '#000000'.

steps.title: Create the handleColorChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your ColorPicker component, define a function called handleColorChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the color state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: Remember to use the setColor function from useState to update the state. The function should have a parameter typed as React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleColorChange function is defined inside the component, ready to be connected to an input element in later steps.
successCriteria: The handleColorChange function is defined with proper TypeScript typing for the event parameter and calls setColor with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function has the correct parameter type and updates the color state properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleColorChange function isn't defined correctly. Check the parameter type and how you update the state.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: In your ColorPicker component, return a div element with a className of 'color-picker' as the main container.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (which returns null) with a JSX div element that has the className attribute set to 'color-picker'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX structure with a div element that will serve as the main container for the color picker UI.
successCriteria: The ColorPicker component returns a div element with className='color-picker'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element with exactly className='color-picker'. Check that you've replaced the 'return null;' statement with the JSX div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='color-picker'. Remember to replace the current return statement with the JSX div.

steps.title: Add a heading to the component
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an h1 element with the text 'Color Picker'.
steps.hint: Add the heading element directly inside the div you created in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now displays a heading 'Color Picker' inside the container div.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Color Picker' is added inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an element, but make sure it's an h1 with the exact text 'Color Picker'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Check that you placed an h1 element with 'Color Picker' text inside the div.

steps.title: Add the color preview display
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a div element after the heading to display the current color value. Use inline style to set the backgroundColor to the color state value.
steps.hint: You can add a div with style={{ backgroundColor: color }} to show a color preview.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a value with inline style
Color preview
steps.expectedOutcome: The component should now have a visual color preview area that will show the current color value.
successCriteria: A div element is added after the heading with inline style backgroundColor set to the color state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div element, but make sure it has inline style with backgroundColor set to the color state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color preview display wasn't added correctly. Add a div element with style={{ backgroundColor: color }} after the heading.

steps.title: Add the color value text display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the color preview that displays the current color value from state.
steps.hint:
Use a

tag with the color state variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value as text

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing the current color value appears below the color preview box.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists that displays the current color state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a paragraph element that shows the color state value.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element displaying the color value is missing or incorrect. Try adding a

tag with the color variable inside curly braces.

steps.title: Add the color input and wire the change handler
steps.instruction: Add an <input> element of type 'color' inside the main <div>. Bind its value to the color state and wire its onChange event to the handleColorChange function.
steps.hint: The input element should be placed after the color preview <div>. Use the value and onChange attributes to connect it to your state and handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: connecting an input to state
<input type="text" value={text} onChange={handleTextChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now include a color picker input that updates the color preview when changed.
successCriteria: An <input> element with type='color' is added, its value is bound to the color state, and its onChange is wired to handleColorChange.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the input, but make sure to connect both the value and onChange attributes correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The color input is missing or not properly connected. Check that you have an <input type='color'> with value={color} and onChange={handleColorChange}.

steps.title: Add a label for the color input
steps.instruction: Add a label element before the color input with the text 'Choose a color:' and an htmlFor attribute matching the input's id.
steps.hint: The label should be placed right before the input element. Use the htmlFor attribute to associate the label with the input's id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A label with the text 'Choose a color:' appears above the color input, improving accessibility by associating the label with the input field.
successCriteria: The label element is present with the correct text and htmlFor attribute matching the input's id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a label, but check that the htmlFor attribute matches the input's id exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label element is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add a <label> with the text 'Choose a color:' and an htmlFor attribute.
